flags: Periods where the cards are silent: the later period, as the rules say. Unattributed descriptions are “ours”: lōrum galeae, chīrothēcae birotāriae, volātus dīlātus, aurēs clausae, clāvēs autoraedae, tessera in tēlephōnō, digitō iter dūcere, sarcina manuālis, ē trāmine dēscendere. The bicycle phrases (birotā vehī etc.) are “modern”; adventūra is “modern” for its modern sense (the word is medieval). Classical words for the same thing are “classical” (rota, catēna, vidulus, crumēna, mystagōgus: Cic. Verr. 2.4.132 describes a tour guide; celebritās viae: Cic. Att. 3.14.2; rotam sufflāmināre: Sen. Apocol. 14.3; sarcinās colligere: Varr. RR 1.1.1); vehicle-part senses of old words are “modern” (ōstiolum, fenestella, receptāculum, crepīdō, orbita).
chīrothēca: the card calls it post-Classical; Lewis & Short lacks it and M-O s.v. glove marks it medieval (+), so “medieval”.
carrulus: Lewis & Short cites only Dig. 17.2.52, so “post-classical”. In the libellī it is the shopping trolley (Libellus IV).

canthus: entry-20 says “rim”, entry-274 “tyre: the iron tyre of a wheel (Quint. 1.5.8)”, as Lewis & Short and Libellus VII (canthum rotae posteriōris). The tyre record leads with canthus, entry-20’s pneumaticum second; the rim record keeps canthus as entry-20 has it.
brake merges entry-274 (rotās sufflāmināre, Traupman 215, Libellus IV; leads) and entry-20 (frēnum, frēnāre).

Suspected missing macrons, copied as printed: conscendere / conscende (entry-20, entry-21) against the long vowel before ns (the batch writes cōnscēnsiōnālis, īnscendō); inflāre (entry-20) for īnflāre.

entry-274 cites autoraedam īnscendere to Traupman 215, but p. 215 gives autoraedam intrōgredī for getting into a car; Traupman’s īnscendō in + acc. is for a bus, plane, ship or train. His “get off” is ēgredior dē, not ē trāmine dēscendere.
pharus: “Plin. 18.83” (copied from M-O) is Plin. NH 36.83 (36.18.83 in the old numbering). The masculine follows Lewis & Short’s note on Suet. Claud. 20 and has a note.
genuāle: Lewis & Short has only the plural genuālia (Ov. M. 10.593). vitrum antiāerium has no diaeresis, unlike āë- elsewhere.
